For a fixed user/model, let M be the eligible negative-pool size and A the number of negatives preceding the positive under the declared total ordering. Drawing 99 unique negatives uniformly without replacement gives X ~ Hypergeom(M,A,99); sampled hit@10 has expectation P(X≤9), implemented as `scipy.stats.hypergeom.cdf(9,M,A,99)`, provided M≥99. This is a forward calibration from exact pool rank A+1 to expected sampled HR, not an inversion recovering catalog HR@10. Sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation. [SciPy distribution](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.hypergeom.html), [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

A reproducible diagnostic implementation fixes ties by descending score then ascending item ID (`np.lexsort((item_ids,-scores))`), applying that ordering to both exact and sampled ranks; benchmark reporting must retain the host’s actual tie rule. Repeat independently seeded candidate draws, without replacement within each draw, sharing candidates across compared models. Average hits across draws per user, then users within category, then the four categories equally. Repetitions measure candidate-sampling variability and reduce Monte Carlo error; they do not remove sampling bias. [NumPy ordering](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.lexsort.html).

For paired user-cluster intervals, resample users with replacement within categories, retaining each user’s entire vector of draws and paired results; recompute the macro mean or paired difference, and take 2.5th/97.5th bootstrap percentiles. This proposed protocol conditions on fitted checkpoints and observed draw vectors; it excludes training/search uncertainty. On a prespecified, computationally bounded user subset, score every eligible catalog item to check predicted versus repeated sampled hits. Exactness applies only to those users and that pool, not excluded items or unobserved relevance. [Bootstrap implementation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html).
